selected_evidence.requirement: Persistent config change adding audit=1 to kernel boot parameters
selected_evidence.summary: Located default_kernel_opts in /etc/update-extlinux.conf, added audit=1, and regenerated /boot/extlinux.conf, which now shows APPEND ... audit=1
Captured pre-restart boot_id (b1181481-d371-4b80-b422-69c46e7c2e7c) and uptime (44s) as baseline
Backgrounded reboot command acknowledged successfully (stdout 'rebooting') before the node went unreachable

selected_evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (connection reset/timeout) then came back with a new boot_id (83f0baed-bc0a-49fe-8eb8-43fad52a38e4, different from baseline) and uptime of only 16s, proving an actual reboot occurred

selected_evidence.requirement: audit=1 active on the running (post-reboot) kernel
selected_evidence.summary: /proc/cmdline shows audit=1 and dmesg shows 'audit: enabled (after initialization)' and audit_enabled=1 with no failures, confirming the setting took effect after the real reboot

selected_evidence.requirement: Setting persists in on-disk boot configuration after reboot
selected_evidence.summary: Post-reboot check confirms audit=1 remains present in both /etc/update-extlinux.conf and /boot/extlinux.conf, and no audit failure messages appear in dmesg
